0.long_answer: The technique described is reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). In RT-PCR, the RNA from the SARS-CoV-2 virus is first reverse transcribed into complementary DNA (cDNA) by the enzyme reverse transcriptase. The cDNA is then amplified using polymerase chain reaction (PCR), which involves repeated cycles of heating and cooling — this is the thermal cycling process. This amplification allows for the detection of the virus in a sample non-quantitatively. It is a critical diagnostic tool that has been widely used during the COVID-19 pandemic.
